<header class="dg-head dg-head-section"><p class="dg-kicker">Appendix B <span class="dg-sep">•</span> <a href="index.html">Proofs &amp; Comments</a></p><h1 class="dg-title"><span class="dg-secnum">B.18</span> Properties of <span class="math inline">\(g\)</span> and of the L.C. connection (§§<a class="dg-xref" href="../metric/levi-civita-connection.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_Levi_Civita_Connection">7.3</a>–<a class="dg-xref" href="../metric/curvature-metric.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_Curvature_Metric">7.4</a>)</h1></header>
<p>Throughout, <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{O}, \mathcal{A}, g)\)</span> is a metric manifold of dimension <span class="math inline">\(d\)</span> and arbitrary signature, <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X})\)</span> is a chart, the Einstein summation convention is implied, and <span class="math inline">\(\partial_k F \coloneqq \partial x_k \left\lfloor F \right\rceil\)</span> for <span class="math inline">\(F \in C^\infty(\mathcal{U})\)</span>, so that <span class="math inline">\(\partial_k \partial_j F\)</span> are ordinary second partial derivatives of <span class="math inline">\(F \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1}\)</span>. Components of covariant derivatives along chart-induced basis fields, <span class="math inline">\((\nabla_{\partial x_k} T)^{i \dots}_{j \dots}\)</span>, follow the rule of Chapter <a class="dg-xref" href="../covariant-derivative/index.html" data-kind="chapter" data-label="chapter_Covariant_Derivative">6</a>: one <span class="math inline">\(+\Gamma\)</span> term per upper index, one <span class="math inline">\(-\Gamma\)</span> term per lower index. From Subsection <a class="dg-xref" href="#subsection_metric_prop_parallel" data-kind="subsection" data-label="subsection_metric_prop_parallel">B.18.5</a> on, <span class="math inline">\(\nabla = \nabla^{\text{LC}}\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(\Gamma^k_{ji} = \big( \Gamma^{\text{LC}}_\mathscr{X} \big)^k_{ji}\)</span>, and <span class="math inline">\(\mathrm{Riem}\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(\mathrm{Ric}\)</span> are its curvatures.</p>

## `<span class="dg-secnum">B.18.1</span> Derivative of the inverse metric`{=html} {#subsection_metric_prop_inverse}

```{=html}
<p><span class="math display">\[
    \boxed{
        \partial_c (g^{-1})^{ab} = - (g^{-1})^{ar} \, (g^{-1})^{bs} \, \partial_c g_{rs} .
    }
\]</span> <em>Proof.</em> Apply <span class="math inline">\(\partial x_c\)</span> to the constant function <span class="math inline">\((g^{-1})^{ar} \, g_{rs} = \delta^a_s\)</span> and use the Leibniz rule: <span class="math inline">\(0 = \partial_c (g^{-1})^{ar} \; g_{rs} + (g^{-1})^{ar} \; \partial_c g_{rs}\)</span>. Multiplying by <span class="math inline">\((g^{-1})^{sb}\)</span>, with <span class="math inline">\(g_{rs} \, (g^{-1})^{sb} = \delta^b_r\)</span>, and using the symmetry of <span class="math inline">\(g^{-1}\)</span> gives the claim. <span class="math inline">\(\square\)</span></p>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
```

## `<span class="dg-secnum">B.18.2</span> Derivative of the determinant and contracted Christoffel symbols`{=html} {#subsection_metric_prop_det}

```{=html}
<p>Let <span class="math inline">\(\det g \coloneqq \det\big( g_{ij} \big) \in C^\infty(\mathcal{U})\)</span>, which never vanishes. Then <span class="math display">\[
    \boxed{
        \partial_k \det g = \det g \; (g^{-1})^{ij} \, \partial_k g_{ij},
        \qquad
        \big( \Gamma^{\text{LC}}_\mathscr{X} \big)^m_{mk} = \partial_k \ln \sqrt{|\det g|} .
    }
\]</span> <em>Proof.</em> For <span class="math inline">\(\mathbf{A}\)</span> invertible, <span class="math inline">\(\det(\mathbf{A} + t \, \mathbf{B}) = \det \mathbf{A} \, \det\big( \mathbf{I} + t \, \mathbf{A}^{-1} \mathbf{B} \big) = \det \mathbf{A} \, \big( 1 + t \operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{A}^{-1} \mathbf{B}) + O(t^2) \big)\)</span>: in the sum over permutations, every permutation other than the identity picks at least two off-diagonal entries, each of order <span class="math inline">\(t\)</span>. Along the <span class="math inline">\(k\)</span>-th coordinate line through <span class="math inline">\(q\)</span>, the matrix of components is <span class="math inline">\(\mathbf{A} + t \, \mathbf{B} + O(t^2)\)</span>, with <span class="math inline">\(\mathbf{A} = \big( g_{ij}(q) \big)\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\mathbf{B} = \big( \partial_k g_{ij}(q) \big)\)</span>, and the derivative at <span class="math inline">\(t = 0\)</span> gives the first formula (Jacobi’s formula). For the second, contracting the Christoffel symbols, <span class="math display">\[
    \big( \Gamma^{\text{LC}}_\mathscr{X} \big)^m_{mk} = \frac{1}{2} (g^{-1})^{ml} \big( \partial_k g_{lm} + \partial_m g_{lk} - \partial_l g_{mk} \big)
    = \frac{1}{2} (g^{-1})^{ml} \, \partial_k g_{lm} = \frac{\partial_k \det g}{2 \det g},
\]</span> where the last two terms in the bracket cancel after exchanging the dummy indices <span class="math inline">\(m \leftrightarrow l\)</span> in one of them. <span class="math inline">\(\square\)</span></p>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
<p>The density <span class="math inline">\(\sqrt{|\det g|}\)</span> reappears in the chapter on integration.</p>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
```

## `<span class="dg-secnum">B.18.3</span> Covariant derivatives commute with contractions`{=html} {#subsection_metric_prop_contraction}

```{=html}
<p>For any connection, contracting an upper with a lower index commutes with covariant differentiation. For <span class="math inline">\(\mathrm{Ric}_{jm} = \mathrm{Riem}^k_{jkm}\)</span>, <span class="math display">\[
    \boxed{
        (\nabla_{\partial x_n} \mathrm{Riem})^k_{jkm} = (\nabla_{\partial x_n} \mathrm{Ric})_{jm} ,
    }
\]</span> and likewise for any other contraction. <em>Proof.</em> By the component rule, <span class="math display">\[
    (\nabla_{\partial x_n} \mathrm{Riem})^k_{jkm}
    = \partial_n \mathrm{Riem}^k_{jkm}
    + \underbrace{\Gamma^k_{ln} \, \mathrm{Riem}^l_{jkm}}_{(\ast)}
    - \Gamma^l_{jn} \, \mathrm{Riem}^k_{lkm}
    - \underbrace{\Gamma^l_{kn} \, \mathrm{Riem}^k_{jlm}}_{(\ast\ast)}
    - \Gamma^l_{mn} \, \mathrm{Riem}^k_{jkl} ,
\]</span> and exchanging the dummy indices <span class="math inline">\(k \leftrightarrow l\)</span> in <span class="math inline">\((\ast\ast)\)</span> turns it into <span class="math inline">\((\ast)\)</span>. The remaining terms are the component rule for the <span class="math inline">\((0,2)\)</span>-tensor field <span class="math inline">\(\mathrm{Ric}\)</span>. <span class="math inline">\(\square\)</span></p>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
```

## `<span class="dg-secnum">B.18.4</span> Moving the metric through the covariant derivative`{=html} {#subsection_metric_prop_moving}

```{=html}
<p>For any connection, let <span class="math inline">\(T\)</span> be a <span class="math inline">\((1,1)\)</span>-tensor field and feed its covector slot with <span class="math inline">\(\flat\)</span>: <span class="math display">\[
    (g \cdot T)(\mathcal{Z}, \mathcal{Y}) \coloneqq T\big( \flat(\mathcal{Z}), \mathcal{Y} \big),
    \qquad
    (g \cdot T)_{ij} = T(g_{im} \, dx^m, \partial x_j) = g_{im} \, T^m_j ,
\]</span> using <span class="math inline">\(\flat(\partial x_i) = g_{im} \, dx^m\)</span>. Then the Leibniz rule holds for this contraction, <span class="math display">\[
    \boxed{
        \big( \nabla_{\partial x_k} (g \cdot T) \big)_{ij} = (\nabla_{\partial x_k} g)_{im} \, T^m_j + g_{im} \, (\nabla_{\partial x_k} T)^m_j .
    }
\]</span> <em>Proof.</em> By the component rule, <span class="math display">\[
    \begin{aligned}
        \big( \nabla_{\partial x_k} (g \cdot T) \big)_{ij}
        &amp;= \partial_k \big( g_{im} T^m_j \big) - \Gamma^n_{ik} \, g_{nm} T^m_j - \Gamma^n_{jk} \, g_{im} T^m_n , \\
        g_{im} (\nabla_{\partial x_k} T)^m_j &amp;= g_{im} \, \partial_k T^m_j + g_{in} \, \Gamma^n_{mk} \, T^m_j - \Gamma^n_{jk} \, g_{im} T^m_n ,
    \end{aligned}
\]</span> where <span class="math inline">\(m \leftrightarrow n\)</span> has been relabelled in the middle term of the second line. Subtracting, the terms with <span class="math inline">\(\partial_k T^m_j\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\Gamma^n_{jk}\)</span> cancel, and by (<a class="dg-xref" href="../metric/levi-civita-connection.html#eq_metric_compatibility" data-kind="equation" data-label="eq_metric_compatibility">7.3</a>) <span class="math display">\[
    \big( \nabla_{\partial x_k} (g \cdot T) \big)_{ij} - g_{im} (\nabla_{\partial x_k} T)^m_j
    = \big( \partial_k g_{im} - \Gamma^n_{ik} \, g_{nm} - \Gamma^n_{mk} \, g_{in} \big) T^m_j
    = (\nabla_{\partial x_k} g)_{im} \, T^m_j . \qquad \square
\]</span> The same computation applies to every slot of a tensor field of any valence fed with <span class="math inline">\(\flat\)</span>, each contributing one term with <span class="math inline">\(\nabla g\)</span>, and to every slot fed with <span class="math inline">\(\flat^{-1}\)</span>, each contributing one term with <span class="math inline">\(\nabla g^{-1}\)</span>. For <span class="math inline">\(T = \mathcal{Y}\)</span>, a <span class="math inline">\((1,0)\)</span>-tensor field, <span class="math inline">\((g \cdot \mathcal{Y})_i = g_{im} \, y^m = \flat(\mathcal{Y})_i\)</span>.</p>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
```

## `<span class="dg-secnum">B.18.5</span> The Levi-Civita connection preserves the metric`{=html} {#subsection_metric_prop_parallel}

```{=html}
<p>From here on, <span class="math inline">\(\nabla = \nabla^{\text{LC}}\)</span>. By (<a class="dg-xref" href="../metric/levi-civita-connection.html#eq_metric_compatibility" data-kind="equation" data-label="eq_metric_compatibility">7.3</a>), <span class="math inline">\(\nabla g = 0\)</span> reads <span class="math display" id="eq_metric_prop_A">\begin{equation}
    \partial_k g_{ij} = \Gamma^m_{ik} \, g_{mj} + \Gamma^m_{jk} \, g_{im} . \tag{B.4}
\end{equation}</span></p>
<ol class="dg-enumerate dg-depth-1">
<li><p><em>The inverse metric is parallel</em>, <span class="math inline">\((\nabla_{\partial x_k} g^{-1})^{ij} = 0\)</span>. By the component rule, Subsection <a class="dg-xref" href="#subsection_metric_prop_inverse" data-kind="subsection" data-label="subsection_metric_prop_inverse">B.18.1</a> and (<a class="dg-xref" href="#eq_metric_prop_A" data-kind="equation" data-label="eq_metric_prop_A">B.4</a>),  <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
            (\nabla_{\partial x_k} g^{-1})^{ij}
            &amp;= \partial_k (g^{-1})^{ij} + \Gamma^i_{mk} \, (g^{-1})^{mj} + \Gamma^j_{mk} \, (g^{-1})^{im} \\
            &amp;= - (g^{-1})^{ir} (g^{-1})^{js} \big( \Gamma^m_{rk} \, g_{ms} + \Gamma^m_{sk} \, g_{rm} \big)
            + \Gamma^i_{mk} \, (g^{-1})^{mj} + \Gamma^j_{mk} \, (g^{-1})^{im} \\
            &amp;= - \Gamma^j_{rk} \, (g^{-1})^{ir} - \Gamma^i_{sk} \, (g^{-1})^{js}
            + \Gamma^i_{mk} \, (g^{-1})^{mj} + \Gamma^j_{mk} \, (g^{-1})^{im} = 0 .
        \end{align*}</span></p></li>
<li><p><em>The metric moves through <span class="math inline">\(\nabla\)</span>.</em> By Subsection <a class="dg-xref" href="#subsection_metric_prop_moving" data-kind="subsection" data-label="subsection_metric_prop_moving">B.18.4</a>, <span class="math inline">\(\nabla g = 0\)</span> and item 1, contracting with <span class="math inline">\(g\)</span> or <span class="math inline">\(g^{-1}\)</span> commutes with <span class="math inline">\(\nabla\)</span>, e.g. <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_\mathcal{X} (g \cdot T) = g \cdot \nabla_\mathcal{X} T\)</span>. In particular, <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_\mathcal{X} \flat(\mathcal{Y}) = \flat(\nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathcal{Y})\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\nabla_\mathcal{X} \flat^{-1}(\mathsf{X}) = \flat^{-1}(\nabla_\mathcal{X} \mathsf{X})\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><em>Parallel transport preserves <span class="math inline">\(g\)</span>.</em> For vector fields <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}_\gamma\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{Y}_\gamma\)</span> along <span class="math inline">\(\gamma\)</span>, with component functions <span class="math inline">\(x^a_\gamma\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(y^b_\gamma\)</span>, and all functions on <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{U}\)</span> evaluated at <span class="math inline">\(\gamma(\lambda)\)</span>, the chart expression <span class="math inline">\((\ast\ast)\)</span> of Chapter <a class="dg-xref" href="../covariant-derivative/index.html" data-kind="chapter" data-label="chapter_Covariant_Derivative">6</a> gives  <span class="math display">\[
            \begin{aligned}
                g\big( \nabla_{v_\gamma} \mathcal{X}_\gamma, \mathcal{Y}_\gamma \big) + g\big( \mathcal{X}_\gamma, \nabla_{v_\gamma} \mathcal{Y}_\gamma \big)
                &amp;= g_{ab} \Big( \frac{d x^a_\gamma}{d\lambda} \, y^b_\gamma + x^a_\gamma \, \frac{d y^b_\gamma}{d\lambda} \Big)
                + \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U} \, x^j_\gamma \, y^b_\gamma \underbrace{\big( \Gamma^a_{ji} \, g_{ab} + \Gamma^a_{bi} \, g_{ja} \big)}_{\partial_i g_{jb} \text{ by~(B.4)}} \\
                &amp;= \frac{d}{d\lambda} \, g\big( \mathcal{X}_\gamma, \mathcal{Y}_\gamma \big),
            \end{aligned}
        \]</span>  by the product rule. Parallelly transported fields therefore keep their magnitudes and mutual angles. For <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{X}_\gamma = \mathcal{Y}_\gamma = v_\gamma\)</span> along an autoparallelly transported curve, <span class="math inline">\(\frac{d}{d\lambda} \, g(v_\gamma, v_\gamma) = 2 \, g(\nabla_{v_\gamma} v_\gamma, v_\gamma) = 0\)</span>: such curves have constant <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(s_\gamma\)</span>.</p></li>
</ol>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
```

## `<span class="dg-secnum">B.18.6</span> The Riemann–Christoffel curvature in normal coordinates`{=html} {#subsection_metric_prop_normal}

```{=html}
<p>Let <span class="math inline">\((\mathcal{U}, \mathscr{X})\)</span> be a normal chart at <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span> (Chapter <a class="dg-xref" href="../covariant-derivative/index.html" data-kind="chapter" data-label="chapter_Covariant_Derivative">6</a>). Since <span class="math inline">\(\nabla^{\text{LC}}\)</span> is torsion free, all its connection coefficient functions vanish at <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>, and then, by (<a class="dg-xref" href="#eq_metric_prop_A" data-kind="equation" data-label="eq_metric_prop_A">B.4</a>), so do all first derivatives of the metric, <span class="math inline">\(\partial_k g_{ij}(p) = 0\)</span>. In such a chart, <span class="math display">\[
    \boxed{
        (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{ajkm}(p) = \frac{1}{2} \Big( \partial_k \partial_j g_{am} - \partial_k \partial_a g_{jm}
        - \partial_m \partial_j g_{ak} + \partial_m \partial_a g_{jk} \Big)(p) .
    }
\]</span> <em>Proof.</em> At <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span> the quadratic terms of <span class="math inline">\(\mathrm{Riem}^i_{jkm} = \partial_k \Gamma^i_{jm} - \partial_m \Gamma^i_{jk} + \Gamma^i_{rk} \, \Gamma^r_{jm} - \Gamma^i_{rm} \, \Gamma^r_{jk}\)</span> vanish, and in <span class="math inline">\(\partial_k \Gamma^i_{jm}\)</span> the term containing <span class="math inline">\(\partial_k (g^{-1})^{il}\)</span> multiplies first derivatives of <span class="math inline">\(g\)</span>, so <span class="math display">\[
    \partial_k \Gamma^i_{jm}(p) = \frac{1}{2} (g^{-1})^{il} \big( \partial_k \partial_m g_{lj} + \partial_k \partial_j g_{lm} - \partial_k \partial_l g_{jm} \big)(p).
\]</span> Subtracting the same expression with <span class="math inline">\(k \leftrightarrow m\)</span>, the terms <span class="math inline">\(\partial_k \partial_m g_{lj}\)</span> cancel by Schwarz’s theorem, and <span class="math inline">\((\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{ajkm} = g_{ai} \, \mathrm{Riem}^i_{jkm}\)</span>, with <span class="math inline">\(g_{ai} (g^{-1})^{il} = \delta^l_a\)</span>, gives the claim. <span class="math inline">\(\square\)</span></p>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
```

## `<span class="dg-secnum">B.18.7</span> Symmetries of the Riemann–Christoffel curvature`{=html} {#subsection_metric_prop_symmetries}

```{=html}
<p><span class="math display">\[
    \boxed{
        \begin{aligned}
            &amp;\text{(a)} \quad (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{ajkm} = - (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{ajmk},
            &amp;&amp;\text{(b)} \quad (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{ajkm} = - (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{jakm}, \\
            &amp;\text{(c)} \quad (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{ajkm} + (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{akmj} + (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{amjk} = 0,
            &amp;&amp;\text{(d)} \quad (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{ajkm} = (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{kmaj}.
        \end{aligned}
    }
\]</span> (a) holds for any connection, (c) is the <strong>algebraic Bianchi identity</strong>, (b) and (d) are specific to <span class="math inline">\(\nabla^{\text{LC}}\)</span>. <em>Proof.</em> Each identity states that a <span class="math inline">\((0,4)\)</span>-tensor field vanishes, so it suffices to check it at an arbitrary <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span> in a normal chart at <span class="math inline">\(p\)</span>. With <span class="math inline">\(\partial_{km} g_{aj} \coloneqq \partial_k \partial_m g_{aj}(p)\)</span>, symmetric in <span class="math inline">\(k, m\)</span> and in <span class="math inline">\(a, j\)</span>, <span class="math display">\[
    2 \, (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{ajkm}(p) = \partial_{kj} g_{am} - \partial_{ka} g_{jm} - \partial_{mj} g_{ak} + \partial_{ma} g_{jk} .
\]</span> (a): <span class="math inline">\(k \leftrightarrow m\)</span> maps the four terms onto minus themselves. (b): <span class="math inline">\(a \leftrightarrow j\)</span> swaps the first two and the last two terms, flipping the sign. (d): <span class="math inline">\((a,j) \leftrightarrow (k,m)\)</span> gives <span class="math inline">\(\partial_{am} g_{kj} - \partial_{ak} g_{mj} - \partial_{jm} g_{ka} + \partial_{jk} g_{ma}\)</span>, the same four terms. (c): the three cyclic permutations of <span class="math inline">\((j,k,m)\)</span>, <span class="math display">\[
    \begin{aligned}
             &amp;\partial_{kj} g_{am} - \partial_{ka} g_{jm} - \partial_{mj} g_{ak} + \partial_{ma} g_{jk} \\
        + \, &amp;\partial_{mk} g_{aj} - \partial_{ma} g_{kj} - \partial_{jk} g_{am} + \partial_{ja} g_{km} \\
        + \, &amp;\partial_{jm} g_{ak} - \partial_{ja} g_{mk} - \partial_{km} g_{aj} + \partial_{ka} g_{mj} = 0 ,
    \end{aligned}
\]</span> cancel term by term. <span class="math inline">\(\square\)</span></p>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
<p>Multiplying (c) by <span class="math inline">\((g^{-1})^{ia}\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(\mathrm{Riem}^i_{jkm} + \mathrm{Riem}^i_{kmj} + \mathrm{Riem}^i_{mjk} = 0\)</span>. Together, (a)–(d) leave <span class="math inline">\(d^2 (d^2 - 1)/12\)</span> independent component functions (not proved here): one for <span class="math inline">\(d = 2\)</span>, six for <span class="math inline">\(d = 3\)</span>, twenty for <span class="math inline">\(d = 4\)</span>.</p>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
```

## `<span class="dg-secnum">B.18.8</span> Symmetry of the Ricci and Einstein curvatures`{=html} {#subsection_metric_prop_Ricci}

```{=html}
<p><span class="math display">\[
    \boxed{
        \mathrm{Ric}_{ab} = \mathrm{Ric}_{ba},
        \qquad
        G_{ab} = G_{ba} .
    }
\]</span> <em>Proof.</em> With <span class="math inline">\(\mathrm{Riem}^m_{amb} = (g^{-1})^{mc} \, (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{camb}\)</span>, (d), the relabelling <span class="math inline">\(m \leftrightarrow c\)</span> and the symmetry of <span class="math inline">\(g^{-1}\)</span>, <span class="math display">\[
    \mathrm{Ric}_{ab} = (g^{-1})^{mc} \, (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{camb} = (g^{-1})^{mc} \, (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{mbca}
    = (g^{-1})^{cm} \, (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{cbma} = \mathrm{Ric}_{ba} .
\]</span> <span class="math inline">\(G = \mathrm{Ric} - \frac{1}{2} R \, g\)</span> is then a sum of symmetric tensor fields. <span class="math inline">\(\square\)</span></p>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
```

## `<span class="dg-secnum">B.18.9</span> Two dimensions`{=html} {#subsection_metric_prop_2d}

```{=html}
<p>If <span class="math inline">\(d = 2\)</span>, the curvature is determined by the Ricci scalar: <span class="math display">\[
    \boxed{
        (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{ajkm} = \frac{R}{2} \big( g_{ak} \, g_{jm} - g_{am} \, g_{jk} \big),
        \qquad
        \mathrm{Ric} = \frac{R}{2} \, g,
        \qquad
        G = 0 .
    }
\]</span> <em>Proof.</em> By (a) and (b), the only non-zero components are <span class="math display">\[
    \rho \coloneqq (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{1212} = (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{2121} = -(\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{1221} = -(\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{2112} .
\]</span> With <span class="math inline">\(\mathrm{Ric}_{ab} = (g^{-1})^{mc} \, (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{camb}\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\((g^{-1})^{11} = g_{22} / \det g\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\((g^{-1})^{12} = -g_{12} / \det g\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\((g^{-1})^{22} = g_{11} / \det g\)</span>, <span class="math display">\[
    \begin{aligned}
        \mathrm{Ric}_{11} &amp;= (g^{-1})^{22} \, (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{2121} = \frac{\rho}{\det g} \, g_{11}, \\
        \mathrm{Ric}_{12} &amp;= (g^{-1})^{12} \, (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{2112} = \frac{\rho}{\det g} \, g_{12}, \\
        \mathrm{Ric}_{22} &amp;= (g^{-1})^{11} \, (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{1212} = \frac{\rho}{\det g} \, g_{22}.
    \end{aligned}
\]</span> Contracting, <span class="math inline">\(R = (g^{-1})^{mk} \mathrm{Ric}_{km} = 2 \rho / \det g\)</span>, so <span class="math inline">\(\mathrm{Ric} = \frac{R}{2} g\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(G = 0\)</span>. The right-hand side of the first formula has the symmetries (a), (b) and <span class="math inline">\(1212\)</span> component <span class="math inline">\(\frac{R}{2} \det g = \rho\)</span>. <span class="math inline">\(\square\)</span></p>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
```

## `<span class="dg-secnum">B.18.10</span> The contracted Bianchi identity`{=html} {#subsection_metric_prop_Bianchi}

```{=html}
<p><span class="math display">\[
    \boxed{
        (g^{-1})^{kl} \, (\nabla_{\partial x_k} G)_{ln} = 0 .
    }
\]</span> <em>Proof.</em> Contracting <span class="math inline">\(i = k\)</span> in the differential Bianchi identity of Chapter <a class="dg-xref" href="../covariant-derivative/index.html" data-kind="chapter" data-label="chapter_Covariant_Derivative">6</a>, <span class="math display">\[
    (\nabla_{\partial x_n} \mathrm{Riem})^i_{jkm} + (\nabla_{\partial x_k} \mathrm{Riem})^i_{jmn} + (\nabla_{\partial x_m} \mathrm{Riem})^i_{jnk} = 0 ,
\]</span> and using Subsection <a class="dg-xref" href="#subsection_metric_prop_contraction" data-kind="subsection" data-label="subsection_metric_prop_contraction">B.18.3</a> and (a), <span class="math display">\[
    (\nabla_{\partial x_n} \mathrm{Ric})_{jm} + (\nabla_{\partial x_k} \mathrm{Riem})^k_{jmn} - (\nabla_{\partial x_m} \mathrm{Ric})_{jn} = 0 .
\]</span> Multiply by <span class="math inline">\((g^{-1})^{jm}\)</span>, which commutes with <span class="math inline">\(\nabla\)</span> (Subsection <a class="dg-xref" href="#subsection_metric_prop_parallel" data-kind="subsection" data-label="subsection_metric_prop_parallel">B.18.5</a>). The first term becomes <span class="math inline">\(\partial_n R\)</span>. For the second, by (b) and (d), <span class="math inline">\((g^{-1})^{jm} (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{ljmn} = - (g^{-1})^{jm} (\mathrm{Riem}^\flat)_{mnjl} = - \mathrm{Ric}_{nl}\)</span>, so it becomes <span class="math inline">\(-(g^{-1})^{kl} (\nabla_{\partial x_k} \mathrm{Ric})_{nl}\)</span>, and with the symmetry of <span class="math inline">\(\mathrm{Ric}\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(\partial_n R - 2 \, (g^{-1})^{kl} (\nabla_{\partial x_k} \mathrm{Ric})_{ln} = 0\)</span>. Finally, <span class="math inline">\(\nabla g = 0\)</span> gives <span class="math inline">\((\nabla_{\partial x_k} (R \, g))_{ln} = \partial_k R \; g_{ln}\)</span>, so <span class="math display">\[
    (g^{-1})^{kl} (\nabla_{\partial x_k} G)_{ln}
    = \frac{1}{2} \partial_n R - \frac{1}{2} (g^{-1})^{kl} \, g_{ln} \, \partial_k R = 0 . \qquad \square
\]</span></p>
<div class="dg-skip dg-medskip"></div>
```

## `<span class="dg-secnum">B.18.11</span> The energy Lagrangian`{=html} {#subsection_metric_prop_energy}

```{=html}
<p>The square root in <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}\)</span> (Chapter <a class="dg-xref" href="../metric/index.html" data-kind="chapter" data-label="chapter_Metric">7</a>) can be dropped. The <strong>energy Lagrangian</strong> is <span class="math display">\begin{align*}
    \mathcal{T} : T\mathcal{M} &amp;\longrightarrow \mathbb{R} \\
    \mathcal{X}_p &amp;\longmapsto \mathcal{T}(\mathcal{X}_p) \coloneqq g_p(\mathcal{X}_p, \mathcal{X}_p),
    \qquad
    \mathcal{T}_\mathscr{X} \coloneqq \mathcal{T} \circ \xi_\mathscr{X}^{-1} : (\alpha \, ; \beta) \longmapsto
    \big( g_{ij} \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1} \big)(\alpha) \, \beta^i \beta^j ,
\end{align*}</span> so that <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L} = \sqrt{\textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma \, \mathcal{T}}\)</span> where <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}\)</span> is defined.</p>
<ol class="dg-enumerate dg-depth-1">
<li><p><em>Its Euler–Lagrange equations are (<a class="dg-xref" href="../metric/length-geodesics.html#eq_geodesic" data-kind="equation" data-label="eq_geodesic">7.1</a>).</em> With <span class="math inline">\(\partial_{d+m} \mathcal{T}_\mathscr{X} = 2 \, (g_{mj} \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1}) \, \beta^j\)</span> and <span class="math inline">\(\partial_m \mathcal{T}_\mathscr{X} = \partial_m (g_{ij} \circ \mathscr{X}^{-1}) \, \beta^i \beta^j\)</span> on <span class="math inline">\((\gamma_\mathcal{U} ; \dot{\gamma}_\mathcal{U})\)</span>,  <span class="math display">\[
            \frac{d}{d\lambda} \big( 2 \, g_{mj} \, \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U} \big) - \partial_m g_{ij} \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U} \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}
            = 2 \, g_{mj} \, \ddot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}
            + \big( \partial_i g_{mj} + \partial_j g_{mi} - \partial_m g_{ij} \big) \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U} \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U} ,
        \]</span>  splitting <span class="math inline">\(2 \, \partial_i g_{mj} \, \dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U} \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}\)</span> symmetrically in <span class="math inline">\(i, j\)</span>. Setting it to zero and multiplying by <span class="math inline">\(\frac{1}{2} (g^{-1})^{km}\)</span> gives (<a class="dg-xref" href="../metric/length-geodesics.html#eq_geodesic" data-kind="equation" data-label="eq_geodesic">7.1</a>). In practice this is the fastest way of computing the Christoffel symbols: read them off as the coefficients of <span class="math inline">\(\dot{\gamma}^i_\mathcal{U} \dot{\gamma}^j_\mathcal{U}\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><em>Its solutions have constant <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{T}\)</span>.</em> Along a solution,  <span class="math display">\[
            \frac{d}{d\lambda} \mathcal{T}_\mathscr{X} = \partial_m \mathcal{T}_\mathscr{X} \, \dot{\gamma}^m_\mathcal{U} + \partial_{d+m} \mathcal{T}_\mathscr{X} \, \ddot{\gamma}^m_\mathcal{U}
            = \frac{d}{d\lambda} \big( \partial_{d+m} \mathcal{T}_\mathscr{X} \, \dot{\gamma}^m_\mathcal{U} \big)
            = \frac{d}{d\lambda} \big( 2 \, \mathcal{T}_\mathscr{X} \big),
        \]</span>  since <span class="math inline">\(\beta^m \partial_{d+m} \mathcal{T}_\mathscr{X} = 2 \, \mathcal{T}_\mathscr{X}\)</span>. Hence <span class="math inline">\(\frac{d}{d\lambda} \mathcal{T}_\mathscr{X} = 0\)</span>.</p></li>
<li><p><em>Relation with <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}\)</span>.</em> Where <span class="math inline">\(\textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma \neq 0\)</span>, <span class="math inline">\(\partial \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X} = \textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma \, \partial \mathcal{T}_\mathscr{X} / (2 \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X})\)</span> for every slot, and <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X} = s_\gamma\)</span> along the curve, so  <span class="math display">\[
            \frac{d}{d\lambda} \big[ \partial_{d+m} \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X} \big] - \partial_m \mathcal{L}_\mathscr{X}
            = \frac{\textrm{\runic ᛇ}_\gamma}{2 s_\gamma} \Big( \frac{d}{d\lambda} \big[ \partial_{d+m} \mathcal{T}_\mathscr{X} \big] - \partial_m \mathcal{T}_\mathscr{X}
            - \frac{s_\gamma'}{s_\gamma} \, \partial_{d+m} \mathcal{T}_\mathscr{X} \Big).
        \]</span>  For constant speed both sets of equations coincide, and by item 2 every solution for <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{T}\)</span> has constant speed. The solutions for <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{T}\)</span> are thus the constant-speed geodesics and the null geodesics (<span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{T} = 0\)</span>, where <span class="math inline">\(\mathcal{L}\)</span> is not differentiable). The price is that <span class="math inline">\(\int \mathcal{T}\)</span>, unlike <span class="math inline">\(L_{[a,b]}\)</span>, depends on the parametrization.</p></li>
</ol>
<nav class="dg-web dg-prevnext" aria-label="Previous and next page"><a class="dg-prev" href="proof-metric-compatibility.html" rel="prev"><span aria-hidden="true">←</span> <span><span class="dg-secnum">B.17</span> The Levi-Civita theorem (§<a class="dg-xref" href="../metric/levi-civita-connection.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_Levi_Civita_Connection">7.3</a>)</span></a><a class="dg-next" href="support-integrals.html" rel="next"><span aria-hidden="true">→</span> <span><span class="dg-secnum">B.19</span> Compactness and the integral over a region (§<a class="dg-xref" href="../integrals/integration-manifolds.html" data-kind="section" data-label="section_Integration_Manifolds">8.2</a>)</span></a></nav>
```
